title: Flat vs plot: how much land do you own with a 1,000 sq ft flat? (UDS explained)
description:
A flat comes with an undivided share of land (UDS), your proportionate slice of the plot under the building. Formula: your flat's super built-up area divided by the total super built-up area of all flats, times the land area. In Housing.com's worked example (200 flats, 1,75,000 sq ft built on 40,000 sq ft), a 1,000 sq ft flat gets about 228 sq ft of land. UDS should be written in your sale deed and it matters if the building is redeveloped.

Sources: Housing.com UDS explainer, Brigade Group, BankBazaar. UDS varies by project. Some scenes are AI visualisation. Educational content, not advice.

More real estate explainers: https://trueyards.in
